title: The Precise Definition of a Limit
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar

definitions.title: Precise (Epsilon-Delta) Definition of a Limit
definitions.statement: We say lim_{x->c} f(x) = L if for every real number epsilon > 0, there exists a corresponding real number delta > 0 such that for all x with 0 < |x - c| < delta, the distance |f(x) - L| < epsilon.
conditions: epsilon is an arbitrary positive tolerance
delta is a response radius depending on epsilon and c
definitions.explanation: This formalizes the intuition that f(x) can be kept within any specified margin of error epsilon around L by choosing x sufficiently close to c within radius delta.
definitions.keyTakeaway: For any target error epsilon > 0, we can find an input tolerance delta > 0.

definitions.title: Delta Choice for Linear Functions
definitions.statement: For a linear function f(x) = mx + b, |f(x) - L| = |m(x - c)| = |m| |x - c|. Choosing delta = epsilon / |m| guarantees |f(x) - L| < epsilon.
conditions: If m = 0, any delta > 0 works because |f(x) - L| = 0 < epsilon
definitions.explanation: The linearity ensures a constant scale factor between input variations and output variations.
definitions.keyTakeaway: For linear functions, delta is directly proportional to epsilon: delta = epsilon / |m|.
